data.summary: tests/test_review_parallel.py::test_a_command_reviewers_losing_copy_is_killed is racy: the losing copy writes its pid with 'echo $$ > pid' (truncate, then write) after mkdir, and the winning copy answers at once, so the review can return and cancel the loser between the truncate and the write; the test then reads '' -> ValueError. Seen 2026-10-01 in the pre-push hook (1 failed, 2642 passed). The product behaviour held (REVIEWED, in time).

data.body: Write the pid atomically (tmp + mv) and make the winning copy answer only once the pid file exists, so the review cannot return before the loser's pid is on disk. Test-only change. Blocks the operator's git push (pre-push runs the suite).
data.title: The hedged-reviewer kill test cannot race its own pid file (fixes bug B-flaky-hedge-pidfile)

data.claim: The test races itself: the loser truncates the pid file before writing it while the winner answers immediately, so the review can return and cancel the loser in between; the product behaviour is correct
data.falsifier: The old script still passes with a 0.5 s delay before the pid write, or the fixed one fails
data.probe: pytest the old script parametrized slow_pid_write=[0,0.5]; then the fixed one with --count 40 -n 48
data.probe_output: old: 1 failed ([0.5]: empty/missing pid), 1 passed; fixed: 80 passed in 5.79s
data.question: Why did test_a_command_reviewers_losing_copy_is_killed read an empty pid file?
